title: CONGENITAL MYOPATHY 10B, MILD VARIANT
alt_titles: MYOPATHY, AREFLEXIA, RESPIRATORY DISTRESS, AND DYSPHAGIA, EARLY-ONSET, MILD VARIANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that the mild variant of congenital myopathy-10 (CMYO10B) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEGF10 gene (612453) on chromosome 5q23.2.

checks.claim: The mild variant of congenital myopathy-10 (CMYO10B) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEGF10 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: patients displaying a less severe phenotype, with later respiratory failure and minicores on muscle biopsy (mvEMARDD or with minicore myopathy), harbour homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants affecting the cysteine in the EGF-like domain.
checks.explanation: The paper says the mild variant (mvEMARDD) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous MEGF10 variants. It also reports a homozygous p.Cys699Ser variant in a patient with mvEMARDD. CMYO10B is OMIM's name for this mild variant.

checks.claim: The MEGF10 gene is located on chromosome 5q23.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing led to the identification of the homozygous variant (NM_001256545.2): c.2096G > C (p.Cys699Ser) in the MEGF10 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper never states where MEGF10 is located. The 5q23.2 location is standard OMIM nomenclature added to the gene the paper names, so under the instructions it counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Congenital myopathy-10B (CMYO10B) is an autosomal recessive muscle disorder. Boyden et al. (2012) found it to be milder than the previously reported severe MEGF10-related myopathy. In their patients, weakness was mainly axial and proximal and was present by 12 months of age. The patients also had scoliosis and joint contractures or hyperlaxity, and muscle biopsy showed minicores. Harris et al. (2018) noted that respiratory insufficiency may not appear until adulthood.

checks.claim: Congenital myopathy-10B (CMYO10B) is an autosomal recessive muscle disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: three of four siblings were affected with an unclassified autosomal recessive myopathy
checks.explanation: Paper describes autosomal recessive myopathy.

checks.claim: CMYO10B is milder than the previously reported severe MEGF10-related myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotypes described therein are generally similar to those of families 1030 and 105, but are more severe.
checks.explanation: Previously reported null-mutation myopathy was more severe.

checks.claim: In patients with CMYO10B reported by Boyden et al. (2012), weakness was mainly axial and proximal.
checks.evidence_quote: Weakness was present throughout the body but was primarily axial and proximal and stabilized in adolescence.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In patients with CMYO10B reported by Boyden et al. (2012), weakness was present by 12 months of age.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected members of family 1030 presented with weakness by 12 months of age, initially in the neck.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients with CMYO10B reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had scoliosis.
checks.evidence_quote: All three patients had childhood onset scoliosis and were treated with spinal fusion surgery
checks.explanation: Stated; patient 105-1 also had mild scoliosis.

checks.claim: Patients with CMYO10B reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had joint contractures or joint hyperlaxity.
checks.evidence_quote: Contractures of the neck were observed in infancy, and contractures of the elbows, knees, and heel cords developed by adulthood.
checks.explanation: Family 1030 had contractures. Patient 105-1 had hyperflexible joints.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in patients with CMYO10B reported by Boyden et al. (2012) showed minicores.
checks.evidence_quote: However, moth-eaten fibers and minicores were also observed, suggestive of a congenital myopathy.
checks.explanation: Minicores were seen in family 1030 and confirmed by EM in 105-1.

checks.claim: In CMYO10B, respiratory insufficiency may not appear until adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas with 2 missense mutations, respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years old or much later, as in the patient reported here. Our findings expand the phenotype of MEGF10 mutations to include onset in the 5th decade
checks.explanation: The patient developed respiratory failure in his 50s. This shows that respiratory involvement can begin in adulthood.

paragraphs.text: Harris et al. (2018) discussed the spectrum of MEGF10-related disease. Takayama et al. (2016) noted that MEGF10 mutations were known to cause both early-onset myopathy characterized by areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD), which is the more severe phenotype, and a milder phenotype of minicore myopathy.

checks.claim: Harris et al. (2018) discussed the spectrum of MEGF10-related disease.
checks.evidence_quote: and discuss the spectrum of MEGF10 related disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: MEGF10 mutations were known to cause early-onset myopathy, areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD).
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the multiple epidermal growth factor-like domains 10 (MEGF10: NM_032446.2) gene are known to cause early-onset myopathy characterized by areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD: OMIM 614399)
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: EMARDD is the more severe MEGF10-related phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: are known to cause early-onset myopathy characterized by areflexia, respiratory distress, and dysphagia (EMARDD: OMIM 614399), and a milder phenotype of minicore myopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract calls minicore myopathy the milder phenotype in contrast to EMARDD, so EMARDD is the more severe one. This follows directly from the wording.

checks.claim: MEGF10 mutations were known to cause a milder phenotype of minicore myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: and a milder phenotype of minicore myopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

paragraphs.text: Boyden et al. (2012) reported patients with a recessive congenital myopathy and MEGF10 mutations. Their phenotype was milder than the severe congenital myopathy described in families with nonsense and frameshift MEGF10 mutations. The patients had childhood weakness, respiratory impairment, and scoliosis. Joint contractures were present in one family, and another patient had hyperflexible joints. Muscle biopsy showed minicores.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) reported patients with a recessive congenital myopathy who carried MEGF10 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the satellite cell gene MEGF10 cause a recessive congenital myopathy with minicores.
checks.explanation: Title states this.

checks.claim: The phenotype of the MEGF10-mutation patients reported by Boyden et al. (2012) was milder than the severe congenital myopathy described in families with nonsense and frameshift MEGF10 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Nonsense and frameshift mutations in MEGF10 were recently determined to be the cause of a severe congenital myopathy
checks.explanation: The paper goes on to say those phenotypes were 'more severe' than in families 1030 and 105.

checks.claim: The patients with congenital myopathy reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had weakness in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: Three siblings from a non-consanguineous nuclear family (1030) presented with childhood weakness, respiratory problems, and scoliosis.
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: The patients with congenital myopathy reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had respiratory impairment.
checks.evidence_quote: Three siblings from a non-consanguineous nuclear family (1030) presented with childhood weakness, respiratory problems, and scoliosis.
checks.explanation: True for family 1030. Patient 105-1 had pulmonary infections but 'reported no chronic breathing problems and breathed unassisted at night.'

checks.claim: The patients with congenital myopathy reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had scoliosis.
checks.evidence_quote: All three patients had childhood onset scoliosis and were treated with spinal fusion surgery
checks.explanation: Family 1030; 105-1 also had mild scoliosis.

checks.claim: Joint contractures were present in one family with MEGF10-related congenital myopathy reported by Boyden et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: Contractures of the neck were observed in infancy, and contractures of the elbows, knees, and heel cords developed by adulthood.
checks.explanation: Family 1030 had contractures.

checks.claim: Another patient with MEGF10-related congenital myopathy reported by Boyden et al. (2012) had hyperflexible joints.
checks.evidence_quote: A markedly high arched palate and failure to thrive as a result of poor feeding were noted, as were blue-tinged sclera and hyperflexible joints.
checks.explanation: Subject 105-1 had hyperflexible joints.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in the patients with MEGF10-related congenital myopathy reported by Boyden et al. (2012) showed minicores.
checks.evidence_quote: Electron microscopy showed focal areas of Z-band disarray devoid of mitochondria and extending across a few sarcomeres in the longitudinal axis, confirming the presence of minicores.
checks.explanation: Minicores were reported in both family 1030 and 105-1.

paragraphs.text: Harris et al. (2018) reported a 66-year-old man with a 20-year history of progressive proximal and distal weakness of the upper and lower limbs. They noted that in patients with 2 missense mutations, respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years of age or much later, as it did in their patient.

checks.claim: Harris et al. (2018) reported a 66-year-old man with MEGF10-related myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We undertook exome sequencing in a 66 year old male with a 20 year history of progressive proximal and distal weakness
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing found compound MEGF10 mutations in a 66-year-old man with myopathy.

checks.claim: The 66-year-old man reported by Harris et al. (2018) had a 20-year history of progressive proximal and distal weakness of the upper and lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: a 66 year old male with a 20 year history of progressive proximal and distal weakness of upper and lower limbs
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: In patients with 2 MEGF10 missense mutations, respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years of age or much later.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas with 2 missense mutations, respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years old or much later
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The 66-year-old man reported by Harris et al. (2018) developed respiratory dysfunction at 10 years of age or much later.
checks.evidence_quote: respiratory dysfunction occurs at 10 years old or much later, as in the patient reported here
checks.explanation: The paper says the patient fits this pattern. The abstract also states that he developed respiratory failure in his 50s.

paragraphs.text: In the family reported by Boyden et al. (2012), the transmission pattern of CMYO10B was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: In the family with CMYO10B reported by Boyden et al. (2012), the transmission pattern was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We ascertained a non-consanguineous Caucasian family of mixed European ancestry in which three of four siblings had an undiagnosed autosomal recessive myopathy
checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive, with compound heterozygous mutations segregating.

paragraphs.text: In the affected members of a family with a congenital myopathy with minicores, Boyden et al. (2012) found compound heterozygous missense mutations in the MEGF10 gene. In a second patient they identified only a single heterozygous mutation. They suggested that the milder phenotype was associated with missense mutations, whereas the severe phenotype was associated with loss of MEGF10 expression.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) found compound heterozygous missense mutations in the MEGF10 gene in the affected members of a family with congenital myopathy with minicores.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected subjects were compound heterozygous for missense mutations c.976T > C (p.C326R) and c.2320T > C (p.C774R).
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) identified only a single heterozygous MEGF10 mutation in a second patient with congenital myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: One subject was identified with only a single demonstrable heterozygous mutation; subject 105-1 carried a novel c.211C > T (p.R71W) mutation
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) suggested that the milder MEGF10-related myopathy phenotype was associated with missense mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: This difference is consistent with the total loss of detectable MEGF10 expression observed in the reported families, compared to the expected misfolding of MEGF10 protein due to disruption of disulfide bonds in family 1030.
checks.explanation: Milder phenotype attributed to missense mutations with possible residual function.

checks.claim: Boyden et al. (2012) suggested that the severe MEGF10-related myopathy phenotype was associated with loss of MEGF10 expression.
checks.evidence_quote: This difference is consistent with the total loss of detectable MEGF10 expression observed in the reported families
checks.explanation: Severe phenotype linked to loss of expression.

paragraphs.text: Boyden et al. (2012) noted that patients with the milder myopathy carried at least one missense mutation in MEGF10. In contrast, patients with the severe phenotype usually had biallelic mutations predicted to cause loss of function.

checks.claim: Patients with the milder MEGF10-related myopathy carried at least one missense mutation in MEGF10.
checks.evidence_quote: minicores were not noted in the biopsies from the reported families with null mutations but were a prominent feature in our patients with missense mutations.
checks.explanation: Follows from the patients reported (family 1030 had two missense mutations; 105-1 had one), but the paper does not state it explicitly as a general rule.

checks.claim: Patients with the severe MEGF10-related myopathy phenotype usually had biallelic MEGF10 mutations predicted to cause loss of function.
checks.evidence_quote: Nonsense and frameshift mutations in MEGF10 were recently determined to be the cause of a severe congenital myopathy with diaphragmatic weakness, areflexia, and dysphagia.
checks.explanation: The paper mentions nonsense/frameshift mutations and total loss of expression, but does not explicitly say 'biallelic'. One severe family carried a missense plus a frameshift mutation.
